rules.title: Berkeley prohibition on the sale or use of coordinated pricing algorithms to set rents or manage occupancy (BMC ch. 13.63)
rules.requirement:
Two acts are unlawful:
- Selling, licensing or otherwise providing to Berkeley landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in Berkeley (§ 13.63.030(A)).
- A landlord using such an algorithm when setting rents or occupancy levels (§ 13.63.030(B)).

A coordinated pricing algorithm is any analytical or computational process that uses Competitor Data to calculate and recommend rents, fees, occupancy rates or other lease terms for future leases. It does so in coordination between a Berkeley landlord and its competitors, including through a third-party vendor. Competitor Data is nonpublic information on actual rents, occupancy, lease dates and similar data about other owners' properties that is less than 90 days old.

Each month a violation continues, and each unit for which the algorithm was used, is a separate violation.

Remedies:
- The City Attorney may sue for damages, injunctive relief, restitution of illegal profits and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation.
- An aggrieved tenant may sue over landlord use for injunctive relief, money damages and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation.
- A prevailing City Attorney or tenant is awarded attorney's fees and costs. Lease clauses limiting a tenant's fee recovery are unenforceable.

The chapter does not regulate the amount of rent a landlord may charge.
rules.key_value: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; each month and each unit is a separate violation; Competitor Data = nonpublic data less than 90 days old; mandatory attorney's fees to a prevailing City Attorney or tenant

coverage.summary: Applies to all residential dwelling units in Berkeley, to landlords who use coordinated pricing algorithms and to vendors who sell, license or provide them to Berkeley landlords. No unit-count, building-age or owner-type limits. It operates alongside the state Cartwright Act ban on common pricing algorithms (Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729, AB 325), which does not preempt local rules.

rules.exemptions:
Excluded from the definition:
- aggregated and anonymous rental data reports that do not recommend rents or terms
- products used to set rent or income limits under affordable housing guidelines
- information used for project-financing market research, appraisals, or software research, testing or training, where Competitor Data is not used as an input when a recommendation is calculated
rules.effective_date_note: The captured ordinance text states no effective date and no final adoption date. It records only that the ordinance was passed to print and ordered published at the Council meeting of November 18, 2025 (8 ayes, 0 noes, 1 absent). A secondary law-firm alert (DX06, August 2026) gives 'effective January 2026' (month only). Status is in force because the alert, dated August 2026, describes the ordinance as already effective and litigated.
rules.quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described 
in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in 
the City of Berkeley.
rules.conflict_note: Organizer open question: Berkeley's algorithmic ban (ch. 13.63) has two published effective dates. The captured ordinance text (D001) contains no effective-date clause, and the only date in the documents is 'effective January 2026' from a secondary law-firm alert (DX06). The documents cannot confirm or rule out a different date in the ordinance, so the effective date stays unresolved.

rules.source_notes: Official ordinance text (D001) is the primary source. DX06 (Morgan Lewis alert, Aug. 21, 2026; the same article as link-only D002) says RealPage, Inc. v. City of Berkeley (N.D. Cal.) was voluntarily dismissed with prejudice on Jan. 14, 2026.

rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance (BMC ch. 13.106)
rules.requirement:
Rental housing providers may not ask about or use criminal history or criminal background checks in advertising, applications, tenant selection or decision-making, for current or prospective tenants. Unlawful acts include:
- inquiring about criminal history
- indicating, in ads, applications or verbally, that people with records will not be considered
- refusing to rent, or terminating a tenancy, based on criminal history
- requiring disclosure of criminal history or authorization to release it
- demanding a higher deposit or rent based on criminal history
- refusing to add an immediate family member because of that person's criminal history
- disqualifying tenants from rental assistance programs such as Section 8 based on criminal history (subject to exceptions)
- otherwise treating applicants or tenants differently based on criminal history

A landlord who takes any action based on criminal history must give the applicant or tenant written notice and an opportunity to respond.

Housing providers must post the Notice to Rental Applicants and Tenants prominently on application materials, on websites and at locations under their control that applicants frequently visit.

The Rent Board administers complaints.
rules.key_value: Administrative fines of $1,000 to $10,000 per violation; civil damages of actual damages or 3x one month's rent; punitive damages; attorneys' fees and costs; injunctive relief; written notice and opportunity to respond before adverse action

coverage.summary: Applies to rental housing providers in Berkeley for current and prospective tenants. Owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units, where an owner of record lives in one unit as their primary residence, are exempt, as are the other listed situations. It operates alongside the state Civil Rights Council criminal-history regulations, which allow limited consideration of convictions.
coverage.owner_conditions: Exempt: owner-occupied property of 1-3 units in which an owner of record resides in one unit as their primary residence.

rules.title: Berkeley tenant screening fee disclosure and ban on non-refundable fees for existing tenancies (BMC ch. 13.78)
rules.requirement:
An owner or agent who charges a fee to buy a consumer credit report and to process an application must give the applicant two statements, either in the rental application or in a separate disclosure before receiving the fee (BMC 13.78.010):
- a clear and conspicuous Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement
- a statement of the maximum fee cap under Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6(b)

An owner or agent may not charge an existing tenant a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy in whole or in part (BMC 13.78.016). This includes fees for a roommate's departure and for requests to add or replace a roommate.

Chapter 13.78 applies to all residential rental agreements despite contrary lease language. Lease provisions that violate it are unenforceable (BMC 13.78.018).
rules.key_value: Rights statement and § 1950.6(b) cap disclosure required before the fee is received; no non-refundable renewal or roommate fees for existing tenants. The dollar cap is set by state law; the Rent Board lists $68.96 as the 2026 maximum.

coverage.summary: Applies to owners of residential rental property in Berkeley and their agents, and to all residential rental agreements regardless of contrary lease terms. It supplements, and does not replace, the state screening-fee cap, receipt and refund rules in Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6.

rules.effective_date_note: The documents give no effective or adoption date for BMC ch. 13.78.

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Ordinance Annual General Adjustment cap (Measure BB 5% maximum; 2026 AGA 1.0%)
rules.requirement:
Landlords of fully covered units may raise the permanent rent ceiling each year only by the Annual General Adjustment (AGA).

How the AGA is set:
- The elected Rent Board sets it by formula: 65% of the Bay Area CPI-U increase, a formula approved by voters in November 2004 (BMC 13.76.110A).
- Measure BB (November 2024) caps the AGA at 5%.
- Landlords with banked (unused) AGAs from prior years may still raise rent by more than 5% to reach the rent ceiling.

2026 AGA (Regulation 1148, adopted October 16, 2025):
- 1.0%, which is 65% of a 1.5% CPI increase for July 2024 to June 2025.
- It may be applied to 2025 permanent rent ceilings no earlier than January 1, 2026.
- It does not adjust rents for tenancies that began on or after January 1, 2025 with rents set under Costa-Hawkins.
- Eligibility conditions and a required tenant notice apply.

Other rent rules:
- Government-owned or -subsidized units registered as fully covered now have AGA-limited rent ceilings.
- For tenancies from February 6, 2024, a fully covered unit may be charged for utilities only if they are in base rent, or separately metered in the tenant's name.
- Rent ceiling increases for capital improvements may be petitioned only for completed improvements, not planned ones.
rules.key_value: AGA = 65% of Bay Area CPI-U, capped at 5% (Measure BB); 2026 AGA 1.0%, usable no earlier than Jan. 1, 2026; banked AGAs may exceed 5% up to the rent ceiling

unverifiable_exemptions: Single-family home whose current tenancy began on or after Jan. 1, 1996 (partially covered, no rent control)
Most condominiums (partially covered, no rent control)

Section 202 or Section 811 subsidized units, and Rent Supplement / Section 8 Loan Management Set Aside / Project-based Section 8 units in projects with a HUD-insured or HUD-held mortgage (partially covered)
Golden Duplex: owner-occupied on Dec. 31, 1979 and currently owner-occupied (exempt)
Owner shares kitchen or bath with tenant and lived on the property when the tenancy started (exempt)
Tenancy started after Nov. 7, 2018 on a property with an ADU where either unit is owner-occupied (exempt)
University rental units such as dormitories (exempt)
Nonprofit cooperative (exempt)
Tenancy began on or after Jan. 1, 2025 with rent set under Costa-Hawkins (not adjusted by the 2026 AGA)
coverage.summary:
Rent control (rent ceilings limited by the AGA) applies only to fully covered units:
- most units in multifamily properties built before 1980
- single-family homes whose current tenancy began before 1996
- rooming houses (single-family homes with five or more rooms rented on separate leases)

Partially covered units are registered but have no rent ceiling: new construction with a certificate of occupancy after June 1980, single-family homes with tenancies from Jan. 1, 1996, most condominiums, and certain subsidized units. For fully covered units the local AGA governs in place of the state cap (Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12 exempts housing under stricter local rent control). Partially covered units may instead fall under the state cap if its own exemptions do not apply.
coverage.owner_conditions: Exempt: Golden Duplex (owner-occupied on Dec. 31, 1979 and currently); owner sharing kitchen or bath who lived on the property before the tenancy began; ADU property with an owner-occupied unit for tenancies started after Nov. 7, 2018.
coverage.other_conditions: Single-family homes are covered only if the current tenancy began before 1996; most condominiums are not covered. Government-subsidized units are fully or partially covered depending on unit type and whether federal or state law bars rent control. The 2026 AGA does not adjust tenancies begun on or after Jan. 1, 2025 with rents set under Costa-Hawkins.

rules.exemptions:
Partially covered (no rent control):
- new construction with a certificate of occupancy after June 1980
- single-family tenancies beginning on or after Jan. 1, 1996
- most condominiums
- Section 202/811 units, and certain HUD-insured or HUD-held subsidized projects

Exempt:
- Golden Duplex
- owner sharing a kitchen or bath
- ADU-property tenancies after Nov. 7, 2018 with an owner-occupied unit
- university rental units
- nonprofit cooperatives
rules.effective_date_note: The original Rent Ordinance date is not stated. The 65%-of-CPI formula was approved by voters in November 2004. Measure BB, including the 5% AGA cap, passed in November 2024; the documents give no single effective date for it. The 2026 AGA Order (Regulation 1148) was adopted on Oct. 16, 2025 and may be applied no earlier than Jan. 1, 2026.

rules.quoted_span: The maximum AGA is 5%. This means that, if the formula in the Rent Ordinance results in an AGA that is greater than 5%, the AGA approved by the Board for that year can be no more than 5%.

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Ordinance just cause for eviction, notice requirements and owner move-in relocation assistance
rules.requirement:
Tenants in fully or partially covered units cannot be evicted without just cause. Measure BB changes:
- Nonpayment: eviction is allowed only if rental debt is at least one month of HUD Fair Market Rent (Oakland-Fremont metro) for an equivalent unit.
- Lease renewal: a tenant may not be evicted for refusing to sign a substantially similar new lease when a fixed term expires.
- Lease breach: the term must be mutually agreed and material; the violation must cause substantial actual damage; the tenant's behavior must be unreasonable; and the prior notice to cease must specify the term and describe the violation and harm.
- Termination notices: every notice must say that advice is available from the Rent Board and give the Board's housing counseling phone number and website.
- Filing: copies of termination notices, notices to quit and summons and complaints must be filed with the Rent Board within 3 business days of service.
- Notice of Tenant Rights: for tenancies starting on or after Dec. 20, 2024, landlords must give one within 15 days and post it in any interior common area.
- Shared facilities: units where the tenant shares a kitchen or bath with the landlord are exempt only if the landlord lived on the property before the tenancy began.

Owner move-in relocation:
- Owners must pay tenants relocation assistance for owner move-in evictions.
- The amounts are indexed to inflation, and the Rent Board must adjust them each year.
- From Jan. 1, 2026: standard payment $19,413; additional payment for qualifying households $6,471. This is a 1.5% CPI-U adjustment approved on Oct. 16, 2025.
rules.key_value: Nonpayment eviction only if debt is at least 1 month HUD FMR; notices and lawsuits filed with the Rent Board within 3 business days; Notice of Tenant Rights within 15 days; owner move-in relocation $19,413 standard + $6,471 for qualifying households (from Jan. 1, 2026)

Only the listed exempt unit types are excluded. Where it applies, it governs in place of the state just-cause rule (Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2 yields to qualifying local just-cause ordinances). State relocation payments are credited against local amounts.

coverage.other_conditions: Owner move-in relocation: the additional payment applies only to qualifying households; the criteria are not stated in the documents. University rental units and nonprofit cooperatives are exempt.

rules.title: Berkeley Ellis Implementation Ordinance relocation assistance for withdrawal from the rental market
rules.requirement: Owners who evict tenants to remove a property from the rental housing market (Ellis Act withdrawal) must pay the same relocation assistance as for an owner move-in eviction. The payments are indexed to inflation, and the Rent Board publishes the yearly increase. From Jan. 1, 2026 the standard payment is $19,413 and the additional payment for qualifying households is $6,471.

coverage.summary: Applies only when an owner evicts tenants to remove a property from the rental housing market.
coverage.other_conditions: The additional payment applies only to qualifying households; the criteria are not stated in the documents.

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Ordinance security deposit interest requirement
rules.requirement: For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on the security deposit at the end of each year. If the tenant moves out before year end, the landlord must pay a prorated amount.
